passages.text: Brothers, my heart’s desire and prayer to God for the Israelites is for their salvation.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to his fellow believers.
Paul cares deeply for the Israelites.
Paul wants the Israelites to be saved.
Paul prays to God for the salvation of the Israelites.
Paul’s heart desires their salvation.
passages.original: Ἀδελφοί ἡ μὲν εὐδοκία τῆς ἐμῆς καρδίας καὶ ἡ δέησις πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν εἰς σωτηρίαν

passages.text: For I testify about them that they are zealous for God, but not on the basis of knowledge.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks about the Israelites.
Paul testifies about them.
The Israelites have zeal for God.
Their zeal is strong.
Their zeal is not based on knowledge.
They do not understand correctly.
passages.original: μαρτυρῶ γὰρ αὐτοῖς ὅτι ζῆλον Θεοῦ ἔχουσιν ἀλλ’ οὐ κατ’ ἐπίγνωσιν

passages.text: Because they were ignorant of God’s righteousness and sought to establish their own, they did not submit to God’s righteousness.
passages.sermon: The Israelites did not know God’s righteousness.\r\nThey tried to make their own righteousness.\r\nThey did not submit to God’s righteousness.
passages.original: ἀγνοοῦντες γὰρ τὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ δικαιοσύνην καὶ τὴν ἰδίαν δικαιοσύνην ζητοῦντες στῆσαι τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ τοῦ Θεοῦ οὐχ ὑπετάγησαν

passages.text: For Christ is the end of the law, to bring righteousness to everyone who believes.
passages.sermon: Christ is the end of the law.\r\nChrist brings righteousness.\r\nChrist gives righteousness to everyone who believes.
passages.original: τέλος γὰρ νόμου Χριστὸς εἰς δικαιοσύνην παντὶ τῷ πιστεύοντι

passages.text: For concerning the righteousness that is by the law, Moses writes: “The man who does these things will live by them.”
passages.sermon:
Moses was a leader of Israel and a prophet of God.
Moses wrote about righteousness that comes from the law.
He said, “The person who does these things will live by them.”
This means that anyone who follows the law will have life through it.
passages.original: Μωϋσῆς γὰρ γράφει ὅτι τὴν δικαιοσύνην τὴν ἐκ τοῦ νόμου ὅτι Ὁ ποιήσας αὐτὰ ἄνθρωπος ζήσεται ἐν αὐτῇ

passages.text: But the righteousness that is by faith says: “Do not say in your heart, ‘Who will ascend into heaven?’ (that is, to bring Christ down) or, ‘Who will descend into the Abyss?’ (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead).”
passages.sermon:
Righteousness that comes by faith speaks in this way.
Do not say in your heart, “Who will go up into heaven?”
This means, do not try to bring Christ down from heaven.
Do not say, “Who will go down into the Abyss?”
This means, do not try to bring Christ up from the dead.
passages.original: ἡ δὲ ἐκ πίστεως δικαιοσύνη οὕτως λέγει Μὴ εἴπῃς ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ σου Τίς ἀναβήσεται εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν τοῦτ’ ἔστιν Χριστὸν καταγαγεῖν ἤ Τίς καταβήσεται εἰς τὴν ἄβυσσον τοῦτ’ ἔστιν Χριστὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναγαγεῖν

passages.text: But what does it say? “The word is near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart,” that is, the word of faith we are proclaiming: that if you confess with your mouth, “Jesus is Lord,” and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the church in Rome.
Paul teaches about salvation through faith in Jesus Christ.
Paul says, “The word is near you.”
This word is in your mouth.
This word is in your heart.
This word is the message of faith.
We proclaim this message.
If you confess with your mouth, “Jesus is Lord,” you will be saved.
If you believe in your heart that God raised Jesus from the dead, you will be saved.
passages.original: Ἀλλὰ τί λέγει Ἐγγύς σου τὸ ῥῆμά ἐστιν ἐν τῷ στόματί σου καὶ ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ σου τοῦτ’ ἔστιν τὸ ῥῆμα τῆς πίστεως ὃ κηρύσσομεν ὅτι ἐὰν ὁμολογήσῃς ἐν τῷ στόματί σου Κύριον Ἰησοῦν καὶ πιστεύσῃς ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ σου ὅτι ὁ Θεὸς αὐτὸν ἤγειρεν ἐκ νεκρῶν σωθήσῃ

passages.text: For with your heart you believe and are justified, and with your mouth you confess and are saved.
passages.sermon:
A person believes in Jesus with their heart.
This belief makes them righteous before God.
A person confesses Jesus with their mouth.
This confession brings salvation.
passages.original: καρδίᾳ γὰρ πιστεύεται εἰς δικαιοσύνην στόματι δὲ ὁμολογεῖται εἰς σωτηρίαν

passages.text: It is just as the Scripture says: “Anyone who believes in Him will never be put to shame.”
passages.sermon:
The Scripture speaks clearly.
The Scripture says this about Jesus Christ.
Anyone who believes in Jesus will not be put to shame.
This promise applies to every believer in Him.
passages.original: Λέγει γὰρ ἡ γραφή Πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων ἐπ’ αὐτῷ οὐ καταισχυνθήσεται

passages.text: For there is no difference between Jew and Greek: The same Lord is Lord of all, and gives richly to all who call on Him, for, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.”
passages.sermon:
God does not see a difference between Jews and Greeks.
God is the same Lord for everyone.
God is Lord over all people.
God gives generously to everyone who calls on Him.
Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.
passages.original: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν διαστολὴ Ἰουδαίου τε καὶ Ἕλληνος ὁ γὰρ αὐτὸς Κύριος πάντων πλουτῶν εἰς πάντας τοὺς ἐπικαλουμένους αὐτόν Πᾶς γὰρ ὃς ἂν ἐπικαλέσηται τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου σωθήσεται

passages.text: How then can they call on the One in whom they have not believed? And how can they believe in the One of whom they have not heard? And how can they hear without someone to preach?
passages.sermon:
People must call on the Lord to be saved.
They cannot call on the Lord if they do not believe in Him.
They cannot believe in the Lord if they have not heard about Him.
They cannot hear about the Lord unless someone preaches to them.
passages.original: Πῶς οὖν ἐπικαλέσωνται εἰς ὃν οὐκ ἐπίστευσαν πῶς δὲ πιστεύσωσιν οὗ οὐκ ἤκουσαν πῶς δὲ ἀκούσωσιν χωρὶς κηρύσσοντος

passages.text: And how can they preach unless they are sent? As it is written: “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!”
passages.sermon:
A preacher must be sent before he can preach.
God sends preachers to share His message.
Scripture says this about those who bring good news.
Their feet are beautiful.
They bring good things.
passages.original: πῶς δὲ κηρύξωσιν ἐὰν μὴ ἀποσταλῶσιν καθὼς γέγραπται Ὡς ὡραῖοι οἱ πόδες τῶν εὐαγγελιζομένων τὰ ἀγαθά

passages.text: But not all of them welcomed the good news. For Isaiah says, “Lord, who has believed our message?”
passages.sermon:
Not all people accepted the good news.
Isaiah was a prophet.
Isaiah spoke to God.
Isaiah said, “Lord, who has believed our message?”
passages.original: Ἀλλ’ οὐ πάντες ὑπήκουσαν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ Ἠσαΐας γὰρ λέγει Κύριε τίς ἐπίστευσεν τῇ ἀκοῇ ἡμῶν

passages.text: Consequently, faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of Christ.
passages.sermon: Faith comes from hearing.\r\nHearing comes through the word of Christ.
passages.original: ἄρα ἡ πίστις ἐξ ἀκοῆς ἡ δὲ ἀκοὴ διὰ ῥήματος Χριστοῦ

passages.text: But I ask, did they not hear? Indeed they did: “Their voice has gone out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world.”
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks about the people of Israel.
Paul asks a question.
He says, “Did they not hear?”
Paul answers his own question.
He says, “Yes, they did hear.”
He explains how they heard.
He says, “Their voice has gone out into all the earth.”
He adds, “Their words have gone to the ends of the world.”
passages.original: Ἀλλὰ λέγω μὴ οὐκ ἤκουσαν μενοῦνγε Εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν ἐξῆλθεν ὁ φθόγγος αὐτῶν καὶ εἰς τὰ πέρατα τῆς οἰκουμένης τὰ ῥήματα αὐτῶν

passages.text: I ask instead, did Israel not understand? First, Moses says: “I will make you jealous by those who are not a nation; I will make you angry by a nation without understanding.”
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the people of Israel.
Paul asks a question about Israel.
He asks, "Did Israel not understand?"
Moses was the first to answer this question.
Moses speaks God's words.
God says, "I will make you jealous by those who are not a nation."
God also says, "I will make you angry by a nation without understanding."
God uses other nations to make Israel jealous and angry.
These other nations do not have understanding.
These other nations are not truly a nation.
God acts this way to teach Israel.
passages.original: Ἀλλὰ λέγω μὴ Ἰσραὴλ οὐκ ἔγνω πρῶτος Μωϋσῆς λέγει Ἐγὼ παραζηλώσω ὑμᾶς ἐπ’ οὐκ ἔθνει ἐπ’ ἔθνει ἀσυνέτῳ παροργιῶ ὑμᾶς

passages.text: And Isaiah boldly says: “I was found by those who did not seek Me; I revealed Myself to those who did not ask for Me.”
passages.sermon:
Isaiah was a prophet of God.
Isaiah spoke with boldness.
Isaiah said these words from God.
God said, “People who did not seek Me found Me.”
God said, “I showed Myself to people who did not ask for Me.”
passages.original: Ἠσαΐας δὲ ἀποτολμᾷ καὶ λέγει Εὑρέθην ἐν τοῖς ἐμὲ μὴ ζητοῦσιν ἐμφανὴς ἐγενόμην τοῖς ἐμὲ μὴ ἐπερωτῶσιν

passages.text: But as for Israel he says: “All day long I have held out My hands to a disobedient and obstinate people.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks about Israel.
God says, “All day long I have held out My hands.”
God holds out His hands to Israel.
Israel is a disobedient people.
Israel is an obstinate people.
passages.original: Πρὸς δὲ τὸν Ἰσραὴλ λέγει Ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν ἐξεπέτασα τὰς χεῖράς μου πρὸς λαὸν ἀπειθοῦντα καὶ ἀντιλέγοντα
